summary: Voice channel, stage 3: the wake gate is live — a Discord voice-channel user can say 「喂 Nora <command>」; the new `voice-wake` service (`deploy/voice-wake/`) detects the wake word with the v3 openWakeWord ONNX, transcribes the utterance through the local `stt` service, and POSTs the transcript to Nora's new `/app/v1/voice/utterance`, where it walks the exact ingest path a typed Discord message would (audit row, Honcho memory feed, engage gate, reactive turn). Ships as a compose service, healthy-but-idle until configured.
details: The wake gate is the only consumer of the stage-2 sidecar's TCP seam: a Python asyncio listener implements the length-prefixed frame codec, conditions 48kHz stereo PCM to 16kHz mono int16 (the int16 contract is load-bearing — float input silently scores zero, measured in the training lab), and runs one stateful openWakeWord model per speaking user. openwakeword is pinned to 0.4.0, the last PyPI release installable on Python 3.12 and the version the lab gated the model against.

The gate is a two-state machine: LISTENING scores every 80ms chunk against the threshold (default 0.5), COLLECTING accumulates the utterance — pre-roll included, so 「喂 Nora」 itself transcribes — until a 1s silence tail or a 10s ceiling. Every chunk is scored even while collecting, because openWakeWord's preprocessor window is stateful: starving it freezes the wake word's features and re-fires on the silence after an utterance (measured: 0.985 on background speech).

STT failure posture is no-wake-no-cost: one retry with language unset (auto-LID instead of pinned yue), then the utterance drops silently. Nothing is queued; audio is transient by design and never stored anywhere on the path.

Nora's side is one route on the existing aiohttp app: POST /app/v1/voice/utterance takes {user_id, text, conversation_id} (text only, no auth — the only caller is the wake service on the private nora network), builds the NormalizedMessage the Discord parser would have built, and hands it to the same Dispatcher.on_message the adapter's listen() loop calls. conversation_id is Discord's flattened "<guild>/<channel>", so a voice utterance lands in the same conversation namespace as the channel's typed chat.

Compose wiring: the sidecar's PUMP_HOST default becomes the `voice-wake` service name (stage 3 made the consumer real; 127.0.0.1 stays as an explicit override for the consume.mjs stand-in), and `voice-wake` ships with no published ports, env NORA_INGEST_URL=http://nora:9100 and STT_URL=http://stt:8000 by service name. .env.example gains VOICE_GUILD_ID / VOICE_CHANNEL_ID / VOICE_WAKE_THRESHOLD; config.example.toml documents [speech.wake] (nothing in the nora process reads it — the wake container is configured by env) and a guard comment keeps [speech.tts] enabled=false the shipped default.
limitations: Inert as shipped: without VOICE_GUILD_ID + VOICE_CHANNEL_ID in the operator's .env the service is healthy-but-idle, and voice answers stay text-only until [speech.tts] enabled = true is an explicit operator decision.

Verified by unit tests (codec against a sidecar-written frame fixture, resampler, gate state machine, real v3 ONNX against lab TTS clips), an integration test (POST -> audit row + Honcho feed + 202), a TCP-seam smoke test, and `docker compose config`; the container image was not built and no live Discord round trip was run in this stage.
The STT container predates the dual-engine server (c84a49cb) and needs a rebuild before the wake gate's model=noise-detection calls resolve against the running service.
